title: Reliability, Incidents, and Disaster Recovery

weeks.focus: Model and freeze user journeys, SLIs, SLOs, budgets, alerts, dependencies, and recovery priorities
Build SLO evaluation, burn alerts, degraded modes, load shedding, runbooks, backups, and recovery automation
Run controlled incidents, data-loss recovery, regional failure, failback, and operator-safety experiments
Decide, teach, evaluate, revise the capstone, and complete Gate 4
evidence: Gate 4 submission and Week 48 capstone revision

readiness_note: Ready on 2026-08-02 after teaching, eighteen deterministic paired trials, six isolated calibration records, semantic and evidence-safety review, authoritative-resource verification, focused validation, and full-course validation passed.

outcomes.statement: Define user-journey SLIs and SLOs with valid populations, windows, exclusions, latency, availability, freshness, and correctness.
Calculate error budgets, burn, dependency exposure, shared fate, and composite reliability and use them in decisions.
Implement multi-window burn alerts and separate actionable journey symptoms from causal diagnostic telemetry.
Build priority-aware degradation, load shedding, bounded dependency work, and degraded regional capacity.
Run incidents with explicit command, operations, communications, liaison, handoff, escalation, and stop conditions.
Produce an evidence-based postmortem and rank corrective work by risk reduction, effort, ownership, and verification.
Verify backup integrity, RPO, RTO, restore, failover, fencing, reconciliation, and failback with controlled evidence.
Diagnose nine reliability failures and defend Gate 4 across consensus, messaging, operations, security, cost, ownership, and recovery.

resources.title: Implementing SLOs
resources.author_or_publisher: Steven Thurgood, David Ferguson, Alex Hidalgo, Betsy Beyer; Google SRE
resources.purpose: Derive a user-centered SLO, budget, owner, and decision policy.
resources.assignment: Read Getting Started through Decision Making Using SLOs and Error Budgets; submit one SLI contract, budget calculation, policy action, and anti-gaming review.

resources.title: Alerting on SLOs
resources.purpose: Derive burn-rate windows, notification class, and reset behavior.
resources.assignment: Read approaches 4-6 and Low-Traffic Services; recalculate one page and ticket threshold and test a low-traffic case.

resources.title: Managing Load
resources.purpose: Reason about feedback among load controls and reserve after failure.
resources.assignment: Read load balancing, autoscaling, shedding, combined strategies, and conclusions; draw one control interaction and calculate degraded capacity.

resources.title: Incident Response
resources.purpose: Separate command, operations, communications, and coordination during user impact.
resources.assignment: Read the complete chapter and power-outage case; submit a role map, first three mitigations, and handoff contract.

resources.title: Postmortem Culture: Learning from Failure
resources.author_or_publisher: Daniel Rogers et al.; Google Site Reliability Engineering
resources.purpose: Write causal, measurable, owned corrective work without blame.
resources.assignment: Read the case comparison, action items, incentives, and tools; rewrite three weak findings and rank five actions.

resources.title: Contingency Planning Guide for Federal Information Systems
resources.author_or_publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
resources.purpose: Connect business impact, recovery order, exercises, validation, and reconstitution.
resources.assignment: Read Sections 3.2, 3.5, 4.3, and 4.4; produce a recovery priority table, exercise charter, and reconstitution checks.

resources.title: Preparedness and Disaster Testing
resources.purpose: Design exercises that reveal unknown weaknesses without uncontrolled harm.
resources.assignment: Read Preparedness and Disaster Testing and the DiRT discussion; submit a hypothesis, abort conditions, and evidence plan.

resources.title: Incident Management with Adrienne Walcer
resources.type: recorded practitioner interview with HTML transcript
resources.purpose: Transfer practiced incident coordination into a runbook and defense.
resources.assignment: Listen to the complete episode or read the transcript; record communication cadence, role boundaries, and two practice prompts.

failure_experiments.scenario: slow dependency combined with load growth
failure_experiments.evidence: journey events, queue/concurrency bounds, dependency latency, priority admissions, degraded output, mitigation timing, and bounded-work invariant
valid/bad counts, SLO error fraction, window rates, burn arithmetic, page/ticket decision, reset behavior, and alert-action invariant

failure_experiments.scenario: healthy components hiding failed user journeys
failure_experiments.evidence: component probes, journey start/end, correctness/freshness/latency results, exclusions, missing telemetry, and journey-measurement invariant

failure_experiments.scenario: conflicting mitigations and incomplete incident handoff
failure_experiments.evidence: roles, timeline, declared priorities, change serialization, handoff state, communications cadence, and coordination invariant

failure_experiments.scenario: corrupt or incomplete backup selected for restore
failure_experiments.evidence: backup identity, manifest/hash/schema checks, isolated restore, constraints, sample workflow, rejection reason, and restore-integrity invariant
last durable version, disruption time, replay point, restored versions, missing/duplicate count, measured RPO, reconciliation, and recovery-point invariant

failure_experiments.scenario: regional loss with insufficient remaining capacity
failure_experiments.evidence: regional capacity, priority demand, reserve, admission, shed work, journey outcomes, measured RTO, and degraded-capacity invariant
epochs, stale-owner attempts, catch-up versions, reconciliation, staged routing, observation window, rollback, and single-authority invariant

failure_experiments.scenario: operator targets the wrong recovery environment
failure_experiments.evidence: source/target identity, approvals, preconditions, audit, namespace isolation, abort/rollback state, break-glass expiry, and operator-safety invariant

challenge_questions.prompt: Which claim in your artifact most directly supports this outcome, and what evidence could falsify it: Define user-journey SLIs and SLOs with valid populations, windows, exclusions, latency, availability, freshness, and correctness.

What unstated assumption could invalidate your treatment of this outcome, and how would you test it: Calculate error budgets, burn, dependency exposure, shared fate, and composite reliability and use them in decisions.

Defend the causal chain behind your evidence for this outcome, including the first likely failure: Implement multi-window burn alerts and separate actionable journey symptoms from causal diagnostic telemetry.

Which reasonable alternative would challenge your treatment of this outcome, and under what evidence would it win: Build priority-aware degradation, load shedding, bounded dependency work, and degraded regional capacity.

What operational, security, cost, or ownership consequence is least supported in your treatment of this outcome: Run incidents with explicit command, operations, communications, liaison, handoff, escalation, and stop conditions.

Where does your evidence stop transferring to production for this outcome, and how is that boundary disclosed: Produce an evidence-based postmortem and rank corrective work by risk reduction, effort, ownership, and verification.

What dissent should a skeptical reviewer raise about your treatment of this outcome, and what follow-up evidence would resolve it: Verify backup integrity, RPO, RTO, restore, failover, fencing, reconciliation, and failback with controlled evidence.

What changed belief or reversal condition follows from your work on this outcome, and where is it recorded: Diagnose nine reliability failures and defend Gate 4 across consensus, messaging, operations, security, cost, ownership, and recovery.
